## Why it matters
- This is the **concrete strategy** behind this author's publishing philosophy already in the vault ([[2026-09-04-systematicpeter-why-publish-research]]): he shares full rules and code because independent readers can then test and run them live (the one-year-later reader email).
- The differentiator is **not the CAGR but the 15% average exposure**: most of the capital sits idle most of the time, so the same notional return comes with far less time in the market — low drawdown (−11%) and high risk-adjusted return (Sharpe 1.79) follow from exposure, not from signal magic. For any replicator, the honest comparison is **return *on deployed capital* vs return *on total portfolio*** — at 15% exposure, 35% CAGR on the whole book means the strategy itself must be compounding spectacularly on the tranche actually at work (or the number is CAGR-on-deployed, not on total — the tweet doesn't say which; first question to resolve).
- Fits the vault's accumulating cluster on **evidence tiers for public strategies**: here the stats are author-reported OOS (self-backtest tier, but with the mitigations this author usually provides — public rules + code). Not yet at the [[2026-08-29-milk-man-replication-metrics]] independent-replication tier.
